newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian reinsurance firm to issue stock.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian reinsurance firm to issue stock.

text.p: Malaysian National Reinsurance Bhd (MNRB), which is planning an initial public stock offering, will use part of the proceeds to finance construction of a new head office building, the national Bernama news agency reported on Thursday.
The public issue of 19.06 million shares at 4.30 ringgit a share will raise 79.56 million ringgit and the shares will be listed on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange (KLSE)'s main board.

The company's prospectus will be advertised around the end of this month, and "we can also expect MNRB shares to fetch an attractive premium when the company is listed on the KLSE in mid-October, 1996," Bernama quoted Malaysian International Merchant Bank Bhd's director Darwis Mohamed Daek as saying.
Malaysian International is adviser and managing underwriter of the company's flotation exercise.
The proposed 14-storey new office building in Kuala Lumpur will cost 100 million ringgit and is expected to be completed next year.

MNRB is principally engaged in the underwriting of all classes of general reinsurance business and upon listing, its issued and paid-up capital would be 189.7 million ringgit comprising 189.7 million shares.

The company presently has 42 shareholders led by state-owned investment fund Permodalan Nasional Bhd (PNB), which has a 50 percent interest. Other shareholders are local insurance companies controlled by Malaysians.
